new-ess-001.mechanism_of_action: Capsid inhibitor: binds to HIV-1 capsid protein, disrupting nuclear import of viral DNA, integration, capsid assembly, and viral release. First-in-class capsid inhibitor with novel mechanism.
new-ess-001.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care. Very long half-life (10-12 weeks) means effects are prolonged.
clinical_pearls: First-in-class capsid inhibitor — unique mechanism targeting HIV capsid
SC injection every 6 months after oral loading — best for adherence-challenged patients
Active against multidrug-resistant HIV (MDR-HIV)
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, St John's Wort) contraindicated
Requires 2-week oral loading (3 tablets daily) before first SC injection
new-ess-001.pharmacokinetics: Oral bioavailability: 21%. SC bioavailability: 80-87%. t1/2: 10-12 weeks (SC). Protein binding: >99%. CYP3A4 metabolism. P-gp/BCRP substrate.
new-ess-001.patient_counselling: SC injection given every 6 months at clinic. Complete 2-week oral loading first. Avoid St John's Wort and rifampin.

new-ess-005.mechanism_of_action: HIF-PHI (Hypoxia-Inducible Factor Prolyl Hydroxylase Inhibitor): inhibits HIF-PH enzymes, stabilizing HIF-alpha, stimulating endogenous erythropoietin production and iron mobilization.
new-ess-005.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care. Monitor hemoglobin and blood pressure.
clinical_pearls: Oral HIF-PHI — alternative to injectable ESAs for CKD anemia
Stimulates endogenous EPO (lower levels than ESA therapy)
Also improves iron mobilization — may reduce IV iron needs
Hb target 10-12 g/dL — slow titration required
Thromboembolic events risk similar to ESAs
new-ess-005.pharmacokinetics: Oral bioavailability: 61%. t1/2: 11h. CYP2C8, UGT1A1/1A3 metabolism. Protein binding: 98%. Renal/fecal excretion.
new-ess-005.patient_counselling: Take with food. Monitor hemoglobin regularly. Report shortness of breath or chest pain.

new-ess-006.mechanism_of_action: Terminase inhibitor: inhibits CMV DNA terminase complex (UL56 subunit), preventing viral DNA cleavage and capsid packaging. No cross-resistance with ganciclovir/foscarnet.
new-ess-006.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care.
clinical_pearls: First-in-class terminase inhibitor — novel mechanism vs ganciclovir
CMV prophylaxis in HSCT recipients (PEARL trial)
No significant myelosuppression — advantage over ganciclovir
Cyclosporine requires letermovir dose reduction to 240mg
Mycophenolate reduces letermovir levels — avoid combination
new-ess-006.pharmacokinetics: Oral bioavailability: 94%. t1/2: 12h. CYP3A4/CYP2C19 metabolism. Protein binding: >98%. Renal (93%) and fecal excretion.
new-ess-006.patient_counselling: Take at same time daily. Dose adjustment with cyclosporine. Monitor CMV DNA PCR weekly.

new-ess-007.mechanism_of_action: Cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitor: inhibits influenza RNA polymerase PA subunit, blocking cap-snatching required for viral mRNA synthesis. First-in-class, distinct from neuraminidase inhibitors.
new-ess-007.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care.
clinical_pearls: Single-dose treatment — superior convenience vs oseltamivir 5-day course
Baloxavir-A resistance in ~10% during treatment (PA/I38X mutations)
Also approved for post-exposure prophylaxis within 48h
Weight-based dosing: 40mg (<80kg) or 80mg (>=80kg)
No GI side effects like oseltamivir — better tolerated
new-ess-007.pharmacokinetics: Active metabolite (baloxavir acid) t1/2: 79h. Hepatobiliary excretion. Minimal CYP metabolism.
new-ess-007.patient_counselling: Single oral dose, with or without food. Most effective within 48h of symptom onset.

new-ess-008.mechanism_of_action: UL97 kinase inhibitor: inhibits CMV UL97 viral kinase, preventing viral DNA phosphorylation and nuclear egress. Active against ganciclovir-resistant CMV.
new-ess-008.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care.
clinical_pearls: Active against ganciclovir-resistant CMV — UL97 mutations
Only oral option for refractory/resistant CMV in transplant
Take on empty stomach — food reduces absorption significantly
Cyclosporine increases maribavir levels — monitor closely
CMV viremia clearance ~60% in refractory cases
new-ess-008.pharmacokinetics: Oral bioavailability: variable. t1/2: 4h. CYP3A4 metabolism. Protein binding: 85-97%. Fecal excretion.
new-ess-008.patient_counselling: Take on empty stomach (1h before or 2h after food). Taste disturbance is common. Monitor CMV DNA PCR weekly.

new-ess-009.mechanism_of_action: Triterpenoid antifungal (first-in-class): inhibits beta-(1,3)-D-glucan synthase (Fks1 subunit), disrupting fungal cell wall. Structurally distinct from echinocandins — retains activity against some echinocandin-resistant Candida.
new-ess-009.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care.
clinical_pearls: First-in-class triterpenoid — oral alternative to IV echinocandins
Active against echinocandin-resistant Candida and C. auris
CYP3A4 inducers reduce levels — avoid rifampin
Dose adjustment for moderate hepatic impairment
Also active against dermatophytes (Tinea)
new-ess-009.pharmacokinetics: Oral bioavailability: 55%. t1/2: 18h. CYP3A4, UGT1A4 metabolism. Protein binding: >99%. Fecal excretion.
new-ess-009.patient_counselling: Take with food. CYP3A4 strong inducers contraindicated. Monitor LFTs.

new-ess-010.mechanism_of_action: Gwt1 inhibitor (first-in-class): inhibits GPI anchor biosynthesis, disrupting mannoprotein trafficking to fungal cell wall. Novel target active against Candida auris and azole-resistant Aspergillus.
clinical_pearls: First-in-class Gwt1 inhibitor — entirely novel antifungal mechanism
Active against Candida auris and azole-resistant Aspergillus
IV and oral formulations available
Investigational — not yet FDA approved
Broad spectrum: Candida, Aspergillus, rare molds
new-ess-010.pharmacokinetics: IV prodrug converted to active manogepix. t1/2: 18-26h. Hepatic metabolism. Renal excretion.
new-ess-010.patient_counselling: Investigational agent — available through clinical trials or compassionate use.

new-ess-011.mechanism_of_action: ARNI (Angiotensin Receptor-Neprilysin Inhibitor): Sacubitril inhibits neprilysin (increasing natriuretic peptides, bradykinin). Valsartan blocks AT1 receptors. Dual mechanism reduces cardiac remodeling and mortality in HFrEF.
new-ess-011.overdose: No specific antidote. Symptomatic hypotension: IV normal saline, vasopressors.
clinical_pearls: PARADIGM-HF: 20% mortality reduction vs enalapril in HFrEF
36-hour washout from ACE inhibitors required (angioedema risk)
Target dose: 97/103mg BID — start low in hypotensive patients
Hyperkalemia risk — monitor potassium closely
Higher angioedema risk than ACE inhibitors (1-2x)
new-ess-011.pharmacokinetics: Sacubitril t1/2: 1.4h (active metabolite LBQ657: 11h). Valsartan t1/2: 6h. Protein binding: 97%. Dual elimination (renal/fecal).
new-ess-011.patient_counselling: Do not take with ACE inhibitors (36h gap). Monitor BP and report dizziness.

new-ess-012.mechanism_of_action: Soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) stimulator: directly stimulates sGC independent of NO, increasing cGMP production, causing vascular smooth muscle relaxation and reducing cardiac remodeling.
new-ess-012.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: symptomatic treatment of hypotension.
clinical_pearls: VICTORIA trial: reduced CV death/HF hospitalization in worsening HF
Start 2.5mg daily, double every 2 weeks to target 10mg
Must take with food — doubles absorption
PDE5 inhibitors contraindicated — additive hypotension
Avoid nitrates — severe hypotension risk
new-ess-012.pharmacokinetics: Oral bioavailability: 45-50% (with food). t1/2: 30h. CYP3A4/CYP2C19 metabolism. Protein binding: 98%.
new-ess-012.patient_counselling: Take with food. Avoid PDE5 inhibitors and nitrates. Report dizziness or fainting.

new-ess-013.mechanism_of_action: Cardiac myosin activator (first-in-class): binds cardiac myosin, increasing actin-myosin cross-bridge formation during systole. Enhances systolic function without increasing intracellular calcium — no arrhythmogenicity.
new-ess-013.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care.
clinical_pearls: First-in-class cardiac myosin activator — novel mechanism
GALACTIC-HF: reduced HF events in HFrEF, greatest benefit in lowest EF
Does NOT increase calcium — avoids arrhythmogenicity of inotropes
Dose adjusted by weight and hemoglobin
Specialist dosing — used in advanced HF centers
new-ess-013.pharmacokinetics: t1/2: 17-22h. Protein binding: 95% (hemoglobin-dependent). Hepatic metabolism. Renal excretion (60%).
new-ess-013.patient_counselling: Specialist-initiated medication. Dose adjusted by weight and Hb level.

new-ess-016.mechanism_of_action: Anti-SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibody: binds conserved epitope on spike protein RBD, preventing viral entry into host cells. Retains activity against most variants.
new-ess-016.overdose: No known overdose. Single-dose monoclonal antibody.
clinical_pearls: Binds conserved epitope — retains activity against Omicron variants
Single IV infusion 500mg over 30 minutes
For mild-moderate COVID-19 within 5 days of symptom onset
Can be used as pre-exposure prophylaxis in immunocompromised
Not a substitute for vaccination
new-ess-016.pharmacokinetics: IV: t1/2 27 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-016.patient_counselling: Single IV infusion at healthcare facility. Report worsening symptoms after infusion.

new-ess-018.mechanism_of_action: Nucleotide analogue prodrug: metabolized to GS-441524-triphosphate, which competes with ATP for incorporation into viral RNA by SARS-CoV-2 RdRp, causing chain termination.
new-ess-018.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care. Monitor hepatic and renal function.
clinical_pearls: ACTT-1: reduced recovery time in hospitalized COVID-19 (10 vs 15 days)
Early treatment most effective — within 7 days of symptom onset
Chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine antagonize remdesivir
Dose adjust for eGFR <30 — not recommended (metabolite accumulation)
IV only — requires 5-10 day course depending on setting
new-ess-018.pharmacokinetics: IV prodrug. Active metabolite GS-441524: t1/2 27h. Protein binding: <30%. Renal excretion.
new-ess-018.patient_counselling: IV infusion daily. Monitor LFTs and renal function. Early treatment is most effective.

new-ess-019.mechanism_of_action: PARP inhibitor: inhibits PARP1/2 DNA repair enzymes. In BRCA1/2-mutated cells, inability to repair via homologous recombination + PARP inhibition = synthetic lethality and cancer cell death.
new-ess-019.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care. Monitor CBC for myelosuppression.
clinical_pearls: Synthetic lethality concept — only effective in BRCA-mutant cancers
Germline BRCA testing required before initiation
Myelosuppression most common — monitor CBC monthly
MDS/AML risk ~1-2% with long-term use
Avoid grapefruit and Seville oranges (CYP3A4 inhibition)
new-ess-019.pharmacokinetics: Oral bioavailability: 30-40% (increased with food). t1/2: 14h. CYP3A4 metabolism. Protein binding: 82%. Renal (44%) and fecal (42%).
new-ess-019.patient_counselling: Take with food. Avoid grapefruit. Report bruising, bleeding, or fever.

new-ess-020.mechanism_of_action: Combination: Atezolizumab (anti-PD-L1) blocks PD-L1/PD-1, restoring T-cell anti-tumor immunity. Bevacizumab (anti-VEGF) inhibits tumor angiogenesis. Synergistic anti-tumor effect.
new-ess-020.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care for immune-related AEs or hemorrhage.
clinical_pearls: IMbrave150: first-line for unresectable HCC — improved OS vs sorafenib
Screen for varices in cirrhotic patients (bevacizumab bleeding risk)
Immune-related AEs: colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, endocrinopathies
Hepatotoxicity monitoring more frequent in HCC with cirrhosis
Not interchangeable with individual components
new-ess-020.pharmacokinetics: Atezolizumab t1/2: 27 days. Bevacizumab t1/2: 20 days. Both catabolized by proteolysis. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-020.patient_counselling: IV infusion every 3 weeks. Report any new symptoms promptly (immune-related AEs).

new-ess-022.mechanism_of_action: JAK1/JAK3 inhibitor: blocks JAK-STAT signaling from pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-2, IL-4, IL-7, IL-15, IL-21, IFN-gamma), reducing inflammatory and immune activation.
new-ess-022.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care. Monitor CBC for cytopenias.
clinical_pearls: ORAL Surveillance: increased MACE and malignancy vs TNF inhibitors (FDA black box)
Vaccinate before starting — especially Shingrix for herpes zoster
Avoid in patients >65, smokers, CV risk factors per FDA guidance
Herpes zoster reactivation common — pre-vaccinate ALL patients
Also approved for UC, PsA, JIA, and RA
new-ess-022.pharmacokinetics: Oral bioavailability: 74%. t1/2: 3h. CYP3A4/CYP2C19 metabolism. Protein binding: 41%. Renal (30%) and fecal (70%).
new-ess-022.patient_counselling: Report any signs of infection immediately. Avoid live vaccines during treatment.

new-ess-023.mechanism_of_action: Selective JAK1 inhibitor: more selective JAK1 inhibition than tofacitinib (JAK1/JAK3). Blocks IL-6, IL-7, IFN-gamma, IL-21 signaling via JAK1-STAT pathway.
new-ess-023.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care.
clinical_pearls: SELECT: superior to adalimumab in RA (ACR50: 45% vs 29%)
FDA black box: MACE/malignancy risk (class effect for JAK inhibitors)
Approved for RA, PsA, AD, UC, Crohn's, AS — broadest label
Once-daily for RA/UC/Crohn's; twice-daily for AD
CYP3A4 strong inducers reduce efficacy — avoid
new-ess-023.pharmacokinetics: Oral bioavailability: 75%. t1/2: 8-14h. CYP3A4 metabolism. Protein binding: 52%. Renal (24%) and fecal (66%).
new-ess-023.patient_counselling: Take as directed. Report signs of infection. Avoid live vaccines.

new-ess-024.mechanism_of_action: JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor: selectively inhibits JAK1/JAK2, blocking IL-6, IL-12, IL-23, IFN-gamma, and erythropoietin signaling. Also reduces COVID-19 inflammation.
new-ess-024.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care.
clinical_pearls: FDA black box: MACE and malignancy risk (class effect)
Also approved for COVID-19 hospitalization (reduces mortality with dexamethasone)
First oral treatment for alopecia areata
OAT3 inhibitor interaction increases baricitinib exposure
Renal elimination 75% — dose adjust for renal impairment
new-ess-024.pharmacokinetics: Oral bioavailability: 75%. t1/2: 12h. Minimal CYP metabolism. Renal elimination (75%). Protein binding: 42%.
new-ess-024.patient_counselling: Take as directed. Monitor CBC. Report signs of infection.

new-ess-025.mechanism_of_action: JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor: preferentially inhibits JAK1/JAK2, blocking myeloproliferative cytokine signaling (thrombopoietin, erythropoietin, G-CSF). Reduces splenomegaly and constitutional symptoms.
new-ess-025.overdose: No specific antidote. DO NOT STOP ABRUPTLY — cytokine rebound syndrome (fever, ARDS, hemodynamic instability).
clinical_pearls: First-line for myelofibrosis — COMFORT trials
DO NOT STOP ABRUPTLY — taper over 1-2 weeks minimum
Cytokine rebound can be fatal — gradual taper mandatory
Also approved for polycythemia vera and GVHD
Monitor CBC — dose-limiting thrombocytopenia and anemia
new-ess-025.pharmacokinetics: Oral bioavailability: 55-70%. t1/2: 3h. CYP3A4 metabolism. Protein binding: 97%. Renal (70%) and fecal (20%).
new-ess-025.patient_counselling: NEVER stop suddenly. Always taper under medical supervision. Monitor CBC regularly.

new-ess-027.mechanism_of_action: Anti-IFN-gamma monoclonal antibody: neutralizes interferon-gamma, a key cytokine driving hyperinflammation in primary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). Reduces macrophage activation.
new-ess-027.overdose: No known overdose data. Single-dose monoclonal antibody.
clinical_pearls: First-in-class anti-IFN-gamma for primary HLH
Only approved treatment for refractory/relapsing primary HLH
10mg/kg IV — weight-based dosing
Monitor CBC, ferritin, triglycerides, fibrinogen
Concomitant dexamethasone often required
new-ess-027.pharmacokinetics: IV: t1/2 31 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-027.patient_counselling: IV infusion at healthcare facility. Report any new symptoms promptly.

new-ess-028.mechanism_of_action: Anti-P-selectin monoclonal antibody: binds P-selectin on activated endothelial/platelets, blocking sickle RBC adhesion to endothelium and reducing vaso-occlusive crises.
clinical_pearls: First biologic for VOC prevention in sickle cell disease
SUSTAIN: 45% reduction in VOC rate vs placebo
14mg/kg IV every 4 weeks after loading
Does not affect Hb levels — only reduces VOC frequency
First-line biologic for SCD with frequent VOCs despite hydroxyurea
new-ess-028.pharmacokinetics: IV: t1/2 33 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-028.patient_counselling: IV infusion every 4 weeks. Monitor for infection. Report pain episodes.

new-ess-029.mechanism_of_action: HbS polymerization inhibitor: increases oxygen affinity of HbS, stabilizing the R-state (oxy) conformation and preventing polymerization under deoxygenated conditions. Reduces sickling and hemolysis.
new-ess-029.overdose: No specific antidote. May cause methemoglobinemia. Monitor methemoglobin levels.
clinical_pearls: First-in-class HbS polymerization inhibitor
HOPE: increased Hb and reduced hemolysis in SCD
15mg/kg PO daily with food
May interfere with HbA1c — use fructosamine for glycemic monitoring
Can cause methemoglobinemia — monitor levels
new-ess-029.pharmacokinetics: t1/2: 27h. CYP3A4 metabolism. Protein binding: 99%. Fecal excretion.
new-ess-029.patient_counselling: Take with food. Report blue/gray discoloration of lips or nails (methemoglobinemia).

new-ess-030.mechanism_of_action: Anti-alpha-4 integrin monoclonal antibody: blocks lymphocyte migration across blood-brain barrier by preventing alpha-4 integrin/VCAM-1 interaction. Reduces CNS inflammation in MS.
clinical_pearls: AFFIRM: 68% reduction in MS relapse rate vs placebo
PML risk — JCV antibody testing mandatory before initiation
JCV index >1.5: highest PML risk — carefully weigh risk/benefit
Withdrawal can cause severe MS rebound — transition carefully
Monthly IV infusion after loading doses
new-ess-030.pharmacokinetics: IV: t1/2 11 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-030.patient_counselling: Monthly IV infusion. JCV antibody testing required. Report new neurological symptoms.

new-ess-031.mechanism_of_action: Anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody (fully human): binds CD20 on B lymphocytes, depleting B cells via CDC and ADCC. Fully human antibody — lower immunogenicity than rituximab (chimeric).
clinical_pearls: Fully human anti-CD20 — lower immunogenicity than rituximab
SC self-injection after loading — at-home maintenance
ASCEND: reduced MS relapses vs teriflunomide
JCV antibody monitoring still required
Pre-medicate with antihistamines and corticosteroids
new-ess-031.pharmacokinetics: SC: t1/2 16 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-031.patient_counselling: SC injection at home after loading doses. Pre-medicate before injections.

new-ess-032.mechanism_of_action: Anti-CD19 monoclonal antibody: broader B-cell targeting than anti-CD20 (targets plasmablasts too). Depletes B cells via ADCC. CD19 expressed earlier in B-cell development.
clinical_pearls: Anti-CD19 — broader B-cell depletion than anti-CD20
N-MOmentum: reduced NMOSD attacks vs placebo
First approved therapy specifically for NMOSD
300mg IV on days 1 and 15, then every 6 months
Pre-medicate with corticosteroids and antihistamines
new-ess-032.pharmacokinetics: IV: t1/2 18 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-032.patient_counselling: IV infusion every 6 months after loading. Report any new symptoms.

new-ess-033.mechanism_of_action: Glycoengineered anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody: afucosylation of Fc region enhances FcγRIIIa binding, resulting in superior ADCC compared to standard anti-CD20 antibodies.
clinical_pearls: Glycoengineered — enhanced ADCC via afucosylation
ULTIMATE I/II: superior to teriflunomide in RRMS
450mg IV every 6 months after two initial doses
One of the most potent anti-CD20 agents available
JCV antibody monitoring required
new-ess-033.pharmacokinetics: IV: t1/2 12-14 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-033.patient_counselling: IV infusion every 6 months. Pre-medicate. Monitor for infections.

new-ess-034.mechanism_of_action: Long-acting anti-C5 complement inhibitor: cleaves C5, preventing C5a (inflammation) and C5b-9 (MAC) formation. pH-dependent FcRn recycling gives 4x longer half-life than eculizumab.
clinical_pearls: 4x longer half-life than eculizumab — IV every 8 weeks (vs every 2 weeks)
PNH: non-inferior to eculizumab with less frequent dosing
Meningococcal vaccination required at least 2 weeks before initiation
Increases Neisseria meningitidis infection risk — prophylactic antibiotics recommended
Also approved for atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS)
new-ess-034.pharmacokinetics: IV: t1/2 50 days (vs eculizumab 11 days). FcRn recycling prolongs half-life.
new-ess-034.patient_counselling: IV every 8 weeks. Keep meningococcal vaccination current. Report fever or signs of infection.

new-ess-035.mechanism_of_action: FcRn antagonist: binds FcRn, blocking IgG recycling back to circulation. Accelerates catabolism of all IgG subclasses, reducing pathogenic autoantibodies (including AChR antibodies in MG).
clinical_pearls: First-in-class FcRn antagonist
ADVANESS: 68% of AChR-Ab+ MG patients improved vs 30% placebo
Reduces total IgG by ~70% — not selective for pathogenic IgG
Monitor for infections (IgG-related immune deficiency)
SC formulation available for at-home maintenance
new-ess-035.pharmacokinetics: IV: t1/2 80h. SC: t1/2 80h. Catabolism: normal IgG pathway.
new-ess-035.patient_counselling: IV or SC dosing. Report signs of infection. Monitor IgG levels.

new-ess-036.mechanism_of_action: Anti-FcRn monoclonal antibody: blocks FcRn-mediated IgG recycling, accelerating pathogenic IgG autoantibody catabolism. Different molecular structure from efgartigimod (mAb vs Fc fragment).
clinical_pearls: Anti-FcRn antibody — alternative to efgartigimod
MYGARD: reduced IgG and improved MG-ADL in generalized MG
SC weekly dosing (weight-based) — more convenient
Reduces total IgG — monitor for infections
Also studied in immune thrombocytopenia (ITP)
new-ess-036.pharmacokinetics: SC: t1/2 8-13 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-036.patient_counselling: SC weekly injection. Report signs of infection.

new-ess-037.mechanism_of_action: Anti-IL-6 receptor monoclonal antibody: binds soluble and membrane-bound IL-6 receptors, inhibiting IL-6-mediated B-cell differentiation and inflammatory signaling in NMOSD.
clinical_pearls: Anti-IL-6 receptor — targets key cytokine in NMOSD pathogenesis
SAkuraStar/SAkuraBento: reduced NMOSD relapses vs placebo
SC injection every 4 weeks after loading
IL-6 inhibitors increase infection risk — screen for TB
Does not require pre-medication
new-ess-037.pharmacokinetics: SC: t1/2 14 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-037.patient_counselling: SC injection every 4 weeks. Report signs of infection.

new-ess-038.mechanism_of_action: Anti-CD123 monoclonal antibody: targets CD123 (IL-3 receptor alpha) on blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) cells, engaging immune effector mechanisms.
new-ess-038.overdose: No specific antidote. Management: supportive care.
clinical_pearls: Anti-CD123 for BPDCN — rare aggressive hematologic malignancy
CD123 highly expressed on BPDCN cells
Capillary leak syndrome risk with anti-CD123 agents
Investigational — clinical trials ongoing
new-ess-038.pharmacokinetics: IV: variable t1/2. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation.
new-ess-038.patient_counselling: Investigational agent. Available through clinical trials.

new-ess-039.mechanism_of_action: Anti-IGF-1R monoclonal antibody: blocks insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor signaling in orbital fibroblasts, reducing glycosaminoglycan production and inflammation in thyroid eye disease.
clinical_pearls: First-in-class anti-IGF-1R for thyroid eye disease (TED)
OPTIC: 83% had proptosis reduction vs 10% placebo
70% reduction in diplopia scores — first effective TED therapy
IV every 3 weeks x 8 infusions
Monitor blood glucose — can cause hyperglycemia
new-ess-039.pharmacokinetics: IV: t1/2 24 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-039.patient_counselling: IV infusion every 3 weeks. Monitor blood glucose. Report vision changes.

new-ess-041.mechanism_of_action: Anti-BLyS/BAFF monoclonal antibody: binds soluble BLyS, preventing B-cell survival and differentiation. Reduces autoreactive B cells and autoantibody production in SLE.
clinical_pearls: First biologic approved for SLE
BLISS-52/76: reduced flare rate and steroid-sparing
IV monthly or SC weekly — SC allows self-administration
Do not use with other biologics — increased infection risk
Also approved for lupus nephritis
new-ess-041.pharmacokinetics: IV: t1/2 19 days. SC: t1/2 20 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation.
new-ess-041.patient_counselling: IV monthly or SC weekly at home. Pre-medicate for IV infusions.

new-ess-042.mechanism_of_action: Anti-IFNAR1 monoclonal antibody: binds subunit 1 of the type I interferon receptor, blocking signaling from ALL type I interferons (IFN-alpha, -beta, -omega, -kappa). Reduces interferon-driven inflammation.
clinical_pearls: First-in-class anti-type I IFN receptor for SLE
TULIP: SRI-4 response 48% vs 31% placebo
Targets upstream — blocks ALL type I interferons
Higher efficacy in patients with high interferon gene signature
SC every 4 weeks after loading
new-ess-042.pharmacokinetics: IV: t1/2 26 days. SC: t1/2 26 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation.
new-ess-042.patient_counselling: SC injection every 4 weeks. Report signs of infection.

new-ess-044.mechanism_of_action: Anti-FcRn monoclonal antibody: blocks FcRn-mediated IgG transport across placenta, reducing fetal exposure to maternal anti-Rh IgG in hemolytic disease of fetus/newborn (HDFN).
clinical_pearls: Anti-FcRn for hemolytic disease of fetus/newborn (HDFN)
REDUX-HDFN: reduced need for fetal transfusions
Targets maternal IgG transport across placenta
Investigational — breakthrough therapy designation
Also studied in MG, ITP, other IgG-mediated diseases
new-ess-044.pharmacokinetics: IV: variable t1/2. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation.
new-ess-044.patient_counselling: Investigational agent for HDFN. Available through clinical trials.

new-ess-045.mechanism_of_action: Anti-sclerostin monoclonal antibody: blocks sclerostin (osteocyte-derived Wnt inhibitor), stimulating osteoblast bone formation AND reducing osteoclast resorption. Unique dual anabolic + antiresorptive mechanism.
clinical_pearls: Dual action: stimulates bone formation AND reduces resorption
FRAME/ARCH: superior fracture reduction vs alendronate and denosumab
12-month anabolic window ONLY — then transition to antiresorptive
Contraindicated: MI or stroke within past 1 year
CV safety signal — monitor cardiovascular risk
new-ess-045.pharmacokinetics: SC: t1/2 13 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-045.patient_counselling: SC injection monthly x 12 months. Then transition to bisphosphonate/denosumab. Calcium + vitamin D required.

new-ess-046.mechanism_of_action: Anti-RANKL monoclonal antibody: binds RANKL, preventing RANKL/RANK interaction on osteoclasts. Inhibits osteoclast formation, function, and survival — potently reducing bone resorption.
clinical_pearls: Most potent antiresorptive agent available
DO NOT STOP without bridging — rebound vertebral fractures within 7-12 months
Must transition to bisphosphonate when discontinuing
Hypocalcemia risk — ensure adequate calcium/vitamin D before starting
ONJ risk with dental procedures — complete dental work first
new-ess-046.pharmacokinetics: SC: t1/2 26 days. Catabolism: proteolytic degradation. No CYP metabolism.
new-ess-046.patient_counselling: SC injection every 6 months. Never stop without bridging to a bisphosphonate. Calcium + vitamin D essential.

new-ess-047.mechanism_of_action: Selective beta-3 adrenergic agonist: stimulates beta-3 receptors on detrusor smooth muscle, promoting bladder relaxation during filling. Increases functional bladder capacity without anticholinergic side effects.
new-ess-047.overdose: Symptoms: hypertension, tachycardia, palpitations. Management: cardioselective beta-blocker.
clinical_pearls: First oral beta-3 agonist for OAB — alternative to antimuscarinics
No dry mouth, constipation, or cognitive effects (anticholinergic side effects)
CYP3A4/CYP2D6 inhibitors: reduce dose to 25mg
Monitor BP — can cause hypertension at 50mg
